sentences.text: 2. In brief, petition averments are; That, on 22-03-2019 at about 7.00 p.m., Lalapalli Venkataramulu @ Venkataramappa was walking in front of M.T. Murthy's Pumpset on Tar road along with his wife from Manchenahalli bus Stand to Buddivanthanahalli, at that time rider of Bajaj Pulsar-150 motorcycle temporarily registered as No.KA-04/TY004216/2018-19 rode the same with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, came from opposite direction and dashed against Lalapalli Venkataramulu @ Venkataramappa.
Due to the impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over his body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Gowribidanur, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Shushrusha Hospital, Yelahanka, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient, but during the course of treatment he succumbed to the injuries on 13-04-2019.
Earlier to the accident, the deceased was working as coolie and also 4 (SCCH-16) MVC 5317/2019 rearing pigs and sheep and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, on account of his untimely death petitioners lost the dependency, love and affection.
Hence, this petition for compensation.
3. Respondent No.1 remained absent and therefore, he was placed exparte.

3(a). Respondent No.2 filed written statement of objections, admitted its insurance policy in respect of motorcycle, bearing No.KA-04/TY004216/2018-19, denied the petition averments generally and contended that within the speculated time respondent No.1 ought to have register the insured vehicle with concerned authority, but it was not registered at the time of accident, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of M.V. Act and the rider of motorcycle was not having valid and effective driving licence to ride the same.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 under Section 170 of the M.V. Act.
For the above denials and contentions it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

1. 2018-19?

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3.

It is averred that the deceased was working as coolie and also rearing pigs and sheep and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
In substantiation of the same the petitioners have not produced any documents.
Hence, no other option but to consider notional income of the deceased in the present case.

Age: 
As per Ex.P23 - aadhar card, year of birth of the deceased was 1961 and so that age of the deceased was 58 years at the time of incident.
Hence, it is considered.
